title: Standard Operating Procedure for Declassification of Government Documents
what_it_is: Standard Operating Procedure for Declassification of Government Documents

sections.label: Declassification of Government documents
sections.summary: The National Archives declassifies Government documents by digitising them, sending them to the relevant agency for review, and publishing metadata of released documents online.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The National Archives facilitates the public's access to the archived Government documents for the purpose of reference or research, subject to conditions or restrictions imposed by public agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The standard operating procedure for the declassification of Government documents is as follows: (a) The National Archives of Singapore (NAS) digitises Government documents in their existing formats, whether they are microfilm or paper records.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: (b) NAS sends the digitised Government documents to the relevant agency for declassification.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: (c) The agency will review the Government documents and decide if the documents can be released for viewing, citation and reproduction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: (d) During the review of documents, the agency will take into account national security concerns, confidentiality obligations and personal privacy considerations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: (e) If the documents can be released, their metadata will be made available through NAS' Archives Online, so that the documents can be made searchable.

sections.label: Public records over 25 years
sections.summary: Public records more than 25 years old become part of the public archives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For the Member's fourth question, as I have explained, the public records which are more than 25 years old become a part of the public archives.

sections.label: Proportion of documents online
sections.summary: A Member asked what proportion of documents appear on NAS Online versus those withheld, and the Senior Minister of State said he did not have that information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the Senior Minister of State be able to comment on roughly what proportion of documents actually make their way onto the NAS Online as opposed to documents that are withheld and are not available online, say, in the past five years?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: I do not have the information that Mr Leon Perera has asked for.
